rationales: Prophase condenses chromosomes but does not align them at the equator.
Metaphase is the phase in which chromosomes line up at the cell equator.
Anaphase separates sister chromatids and moves them toward opposite poles.
Telophase forms new nuclei around the separated chromosomes.
A habitat is the place where organisms live, not a group of one species.
The biosphere includes all regions of Earth where life exists.
A community consists of populations of different species living together.
A population consists of members of the same species living in the same place at the same time.
Hydrogen makes up about 10 percent of the protoplasm in living organisms.
Eighteen percent is approximately the carbon composition, not hydrogen.
Sixty-five percent is approximately the oxygen composition, not hydrogen.
Three percent is approximately the nitrogen composition, not hydrogen.
A.F.A. King’s observations about malaria were not listed in 1880.
A.F.A. King listed his observations about malaria in 1883.
The year 1878 is not the date associated with King’s observations.
The year 1898 is not the date associated with King’s observations.
A phylum groups related classes, not related families directly.
An order is a taxonomic group made up of related families.
A class groups related orders.
A genus groups closely related species.
Collenchyma consists of elongated cells with unevenly thickened primary walls.
Sclerenchyma has thick, usually lignified secondary walls.
Parenchyma generally has thin, relatively uniform primary walls.
Epidermal tissue forms a protective outer covering and is not characterized by this wall thickening.
Lipids are mainly synthesized in smooth endoplasmic reticulum.
Ribosomes attached to rough endoplasmic reticulum synthesize proteins.
Carbohydrates are not the main products synthesized on rough endoplasmic reticulum.
DNA is replicated in the nucleus rather than synthesized on rough endoplasmic reticulum.
Prophase involves chromosome condensation and spindle formation.
Metaphase aligns chromosomes at the cell equator.
Anaphase separates sister chromatids and moves them to opposite poles.
Telophase follows chromatid separation and begins re-forming the nuclei.
Fifty to seventy thousand is far below the stated daily number.
Fifty to seventy lakh is also far below the stated daily number.
Fifty to seventy million is below the commonly cited daily total.
About 50–70 billion cells die each day by apoptosis in an adult human.
Leukaemia is a cancer of blood-forming tissues.
Arteriosclerosis is the hardening and thickening of arteries.
Myocardial infarction is the death of heart muscle tissue due to interrupted blood supply.
Thalassaemia is an inherited disorder affecting haemoglobin production.
Chlorophyll absorbs light most strongly in the red and blue regions.
Chlorophyll reflects much of the green light rather than absorbing it maximally.
Green and red is incorrect because green is not a maximum-absorption region.
Green and blue is incorrect because red is also strongly absorbed, while green is not.
Enzymes are not generally classified as carbohydrates.
Enzymes are not generally classified as lipids.
Most enzymes are not nucleic acids, although a few RNA molecules can act as catalysts.
Enzymes are generally proteins that catalyze biochemical reactions.
Ibn-e-Nafees is credited in this context with first presenting the concept of metabolism.
Wilhelm Kühne coined the term enzyme rather than giving the concept of metabolism.
Emil Fischer is known for proposing the lock-and-key model of enzyme action.
Jabir Bin Hayan is associated with early chemistry, not this attribution of metabolism.
The spindle is formed before metaphase, not during it.
G2 phase prepares the cell for mitosis but is not the mitotic phase in which spindle fibres form.
Spindle fibres begin to form during prophase.
Interphase precedes mitosis and does not form the mitotic spindle.
Species is the basic unit of biological classification.
A genus is a higher taxonomic group containing related species.
A family contains related genera.
A class contains related orders.
